temporal_state_chain.observed: Ethan notices Gary working excessively long hours, skipping meals, and sacrificing sleep. When Ethan invites Gary to a weekend retreat, Gary declines, saying he has too much to do at the hospital.
temporal_state_chain.belief_before: Ethan believes Gary is dangerously overworked and that his health is suffering because of hospital obligations.
temporal_state_chain.belief_update: Yes, but mainly confirming: Gary's refusal reinforces that he is heavily consumed by work, without revealing any deeper cause yet.
temporal_state_chain.belief_after: Ethan believes Gary is overworked and currently unable or unwilling to step away because of hospital demands.
temporal_state_chain.emotion: Concerned, worried, and disappointed by the refusal.
temporal_state_chain.intention: To keep supporting Gary and find a way to persuade or help him reduce work and rest.

temporal_state_chain.observed: During the retreat, Ethan sees that Gary is restless and avoids talking about work.
temporal_state_chain.belief_before: Ethan believes Gary is overworked mainly due to hospital demands and hopes a break will help him relax.
temporal_state_chain.belief_update: Yes: Gary's restlessness and avoidance make Ethan suspect that work is not the whole story.
temporal_state_chain.belief_after: Ethan believes there may be deeper personal or emotional reasons behind Gary's overworking.
temporal_state_chain.intention: To confront Gary gently and learn what is really troubling him so he can help.

temporal_state_chain.observed: Gary opens up about the pressures of managing a new department and the personal challenges he is facing.
temporal_state_chain.belief_before: Ethan suspects Gary's overwork is caused by more than ordinary professional obligations.
temporal_state_chain.belief_update: Yes: Ethan learns the specific pressures and personal challenges behind Gary's behavior.
temporal_state_chain.belief_after: Ethan understands that Gary is dealing with new department responsibilities and personal difficulties, which explains his overwork.
temporal_state_chain.intention: To help Gary find a better balance by prioritizing tasks, delegating, and organizing his schedule.

temporal_state_chain.observed: Over the following months, Ethan regularly checks in and sees Gary making efforts to change. Gary reports that he is less overwhelmed and even had time for a movie.
temporal_state_chain.belief_before: Ethan believes Gary is trying to improve with support but still faces challenges in balancing work and life.
temporal_state_chain.belief_update: Yes: Gary's reports and visible efforts show that progress is real.
temporal_state_chain.belief_after: Ethan believes Gary is making meaningful progress toward a healthier work-life balance.
temporal_state_chain.intention: To continue checking in, encouraging Gary, and offering support whenever needed.

temporal_state_chain.observed: After a year, Gary has successfully adjusted to a healthier work-life balance and says he feels more in control. Ethan sees that Gary can manage on his own.
temporal_state_chain.belief_before: Ethan believes Gary has been improving but may still need ongoing support and encouragement.
temporal_state_chain.belief_update: Yes: Gary's sustained adjustment shows he no longer needs active intervention.
temporal_state_chain.belief_after: Ethan believes Gary has achieved a healthy balance and is capable of managing independently.
temporal_state_chain.intention: To step back from active support while letting Gary know he remains available if needed.
